description: kvmd 4.186's binary WebSocket channel on GET /api/ws, recorded by hand: the capture tool only records GETs, and every frame here is one this client sent. The first byte of a frame is kvmd's operation number, dispatched by exposed_ws(<int>) in apps/kvmd/api/hid.py and server.py. Each input frame is recorded with /api/hid/inactivity read before and after it: kvmd bumps that counter from inside the handler, so a reset to 0 is the device saying it decoded and accepted the frame, and an unchanged counter is it dropping one its validators refused.
safety: Input frames reach the HID. This was recorded with the USB gadget not attached to any host -- keyboard.online and mouse.online were both false -- so nothing was typed or clicked anywhere; the frames chosen are inert in any case (a lone ControlLeft press and release, a wheel of zero, a mouse move to the centre, a middle-button release). The socket was opened with stream=0, so the video pipeline was not touched. Nothing here needs undoing, but re-recording it means sending input to somebody's device, so ask first.

steps.name: ping_json
steps.note: ping over the JSON channel: kvmd answers with a pong event. The latency is a round trip from outside the device's own network, not a LAN figure

steps.name: ping_binary
steps.note: the same exchange over the binary channel: op 0 out, op 255 back

steps.name: pong_binary
steps.note: the pong frame byte for byte, and how many broadcast events arrived before it -- kvmd sends its initial state burst first, so an answer is never simply the next frame

steps.name: unknown_op
steps.note: an operation kvmd has no handler for: nothing comes back, and it logs 'Unknown websocket binary event' on its own side

steps.name: key_press
steps.note: op 1: bit 0 of the flags byte is the state, the rest of the frame is the key name as ASCII

steps.name: mouse_move
steps.note: op 3: the position as two big-endian signed shorts, here the centre of the screen

steps.name: mouse_wheel
steps.note: op 5: the squash flag, then one signed pair; zero steps still count as input

steps.name: mouse_button
steps.note: op 2: the same layout as a key, with the button name

steps.name: key_unknown_name
steps.note: a name valid_hid_key refuses: the handler returns before the HID sees it, and the counter keeps running

steps.name: mouse_move_truncated
steps.note: three bytes where struct.unpack wants five: dropped the same silent way

steps.name: hid_baseline
steps.note: what the HID looked like while this was recorded: a gadget with no host attached, and the jiggler enabled but idle
